claims.text: POL-NS-02 deems a driver to have arrived only where the trace contains at least three consecutive fixes inside the arrival radius, and the radius for this STANDARD pickup (trip_record.pickup_zone_class) is 50 m. The driver's own 98-fix trace never puts him there: derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0, and his closest approach across the whole trace is derived.driver_track.min_distance_m = 53.84 m. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails, the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is not chargeable, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of it. Both the trip record and the GPS trace are COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so nothing in this finding is discounted.

Measuring the waiting period as POL-NS-01(c) requires - from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the 'I'm Here' tap - the driver's in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds (derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec = 0.0, run_count = 0) against the 180 second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180; derived.arrival.thresholds.minimum_dwell_sec = 180 for zone class STANDARD). The shortfall is the entire 180 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, and no driver compensation is payable.

The arrival this fee depends on is the driver's own button tap at 08:11:35 (trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker = BUTTON). POL-NS-12 makes the platform's arrival and wait-timer events a carrier independent of the exported trace only where the marker is GPS_AUTO, so it cannot rescue this arrival, and POL-NS-01(c) fixes the clock to the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix - of which this trace contains none (qualifying_fix_count = 0). A six-minute wait clock started by a tap that the driver's own trace does not corroborate cannot make the fee chargeable.

EV-ADVIS-02744-01 is MISSING: no traffic advisory covers this pickup road in this window (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, payload null). POL-NS-06(i) permits in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a present and populated advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covers the pickup road, and it expressly makes limb (i) unavailable where the advisory is MISSING. There is therefore no lawful-holding excuse and no route by which the driver's intervals could be accumulated; the shortfall stands.

In the alternative, if the Judge prefers to treat the driver as having held position outside the 50 m radius but within 400 m of the pin (his minimum distance was 53.84 m), POL-NS-03 still refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full on those facts. The only compensation route that clause opens is pin ambiguity under POL-NS-03(ii), and it is closed: it requires trip_record.registered_pickup_points of 2 or more, and this trip has exactly 1. The rider named no entrance, block or bay in the chat either, so POL-NS-03(i) does not apply; on this record the driver receives no compensation on any view.

The rider was at the pickup point throughout: her track runs from 08:08:52 to 08:19:08 with 69 fixes, every one of them qualifying, all stationary (speed 0.0) and never more than 13.59 m from the pin (derived.rider_presence.max_distance_m = 13.59, min = 6.67). That is well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius POL-NS-04(c) uses, on every admissible fix rather than merely a majority. A RIDER_NO_SHOW termination under POL-NS-01(d) presupposes a rider who failed to appear, and this record shows the opposite; the driver's statement that he 'was right at the pin' is contradicted by his own trace, whose closest approach was 53.84 m.

POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. POL-NS-01 fails at limbs (b) and (c) on the driver's own trace, and POL-NS-06 disapplies the fee outright, so no driver compensation arises on this record and no profile-based anti-farming analysis is even reached.

The fare ledger carries a single 4.50 SGD cancellation-fee line and nothing else - no base or time fare, no platform fee, no waiting-time line (waiting_time_fee 0.00) - and payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The whole of the contested amount (dispute.amount_contested_sgd = 4.50) is therefore the cancellation fee itself, and under POL-GEN-03 the rider's success on that line is a FULL_REFUND of the full SGD 4.50, not a partial one.

claims.text: The driver's nearest recorded fix lies 53.84 m from the pickup pin and the derived count of fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius is zero, so the driver does not contend that the exported trace carries an in-geofence arrival and accepts that POL-NS-01 limb (b) is not made out on the trace. What those same derived figures do fix is that at least one recorded fix lies within 53.84 m of the pin, comfortably inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling: this is a pickup attempt made at the pin and just outside the radius, to be decided under POL-NS-03 (wrong-position arrival), and not a driver who never came to the venue at all.

The rider's only message is 'ok', sent at 08:13:05, some 70 seconds after the driver's 'here' at 08:11:55. That is an acknowledgement and nothing more: it states no position, entrance, block, tower or bay, asks for no position, and does not say the rider cannot see the vehicle. POL-NS-04(a) therefore fails at its first limb and POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider; the charge cannot be resisted on the unanswered-contact route.

The charged figure is the platform's own: fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee of SGD 4.50 equals trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd for this trip, so the fare line is not defective under POL-NS-08(d) and there is no arithmetic basis on which to reduce it. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check also does not trip on the only two figures that clause names - driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 it requires, and 2 of driver_profile.completed_trips_30d (91) is a rate of 0.022, below its 0.08 threshold - so no withholding is available, and if the fee stands the driver's payout is 80 per cent of SGD 4.50, that is SGD 3.60.

Nothing in the derived trace summary supports a false-arrival finding against the driver under POL-NS-05. The summary reports his closest approach across the whole trace as 53.84 m - inside the 300 m leash POL-NS-05 uses - and reports no distance and no speed at the 08:11:35 arrival marker at all; the marker was thrown 9.2 minutes after assignment against a 9 minute platform estimate, and from that tap to the cancellation at 08:17:36 the record spans 361 seconds. The POL-NS-05 trigger is not established on the derived facts, and no false-arrival event should be recorded against the driver.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute is about the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02744 after the driver cancelled at 08:17:36 under the reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW.

The fee is chargeable only if all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold. Two of them fail on the driver's own evidence. Condition (b) requires the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02744) to place the driver inside the pickup geofence, which POL-NS-02 sets at 50 m for this STANDARD pickup (trip_record.pickup_zone_class in EV-TRIP-02744): at least three consecutive fixes inside 50 m, each accurate to 25 m or better. That trace is COMPLETE, 98 fixes at a 10-second cadence with no gaps, and the derived count of qualifying in-radius fixes is 0; the driver's closest approach anywhere in the trace is 53.84 m. Condition (c) requires an in-geofence dwell of at least the 180-second free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180), measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix; that dwell is 0 seconds. The 'I'm Here' button press at 08:11:35 does not start that clock: POL-NS-01(c) runs it from the GPS fix, and POL-NS-12, which lets the platform's own arrival and wait-timer events stand in for the trace, applies only where trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is GPS_AUTO, and here it is BUTTON. The six-minute wait timer therefore records a tap, not an arrival, and there is no reading of the trace on which this fee is earned.

POL-NS-05 (false arrival marker) is not established either way and I make no finding under it. The derived facts report no distance and no speed for the driver at the 08:11:35 marker, so the clause's trigger - more than 300 m from the pin, or 15 km/h or more, at the marker's timestamp - cannot be tested. The 53.84 m figure the Driver Advocate relies on is the minimum across the whole trace, not the position at the marker; it is well inside POL-NS-05's 300 m leash, but it neither proves nor disproves a false marker at 08:11:35. Because no false-arrival finding is made, no POL-NS-05(ii) referral is recorded; a referral exists only where a clause produces one.

On the Driver Advocate's submission that this is a POL-NS-03 wrong-position case: accepted to this extent. A closest approach of 53.84 m lies outside the 50 m radius but inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, so on the driver's own account he came to the venue and held just outside the radius rather than never arriving. That does not change the money. POL-NS-03 refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full, and its only two compensation routes are closed on this record. Route (i) needs the rider to have given the correct entrance, block, tower or bay in the chat log and the driver not to have moved to it, and the chat (EV-CHAT-02744) holds only the driver's 'here' at 08:11:55 and the rider's 'ok' at 08:13:05 - no sub-location from either party. Route (ii) needs trip_record.registered_pickup_points of 2 or more, and this trip registers exactly 1. The Rider Advocate reached the same conclusion in the alternative, and it is right. Switching to POL-NS-02 makes no difference: where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before the cancellation, the driver never arrived, limb (b) fails, and the fee is refunded in full. Both routes land on a full refund and neither produces driver compensation, so the choice between them does not affect the outcome.

Under POL-NS-06 the same result follows from the arithmetic: the effective dwell is 0 seconds against the 180-second minimum, so the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied to messages. The one route by which the driver could have accumulated separate in-geofence intervals - POL-NS-06(i) - is closed: the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02744-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, payload null), and the clause makes limb (i) unavailable where the advisory is missing. There is therefore no lawful-holding excuse and no accumulation.

POL-NS-04 does not need to be reached, and it does not exonerate the rider: her only message, 'ok' at 08:13:05, names no position, entrance, block, tower or bay, asks for the driver's position, and does not say she cannot see the vehicle, so limb (a) fails at its first requirement. That does not matter, because the refund follows from the driver's trace, not from this clause. The Rider Advocate's further point that the rider was at the pickup point throughout is factually supported - EV-GPS-02744's rider_presence block shows 69 fixes, every one qualifying, all stationary, never more than 13.59 m from the pin - and it sits badly with a RIDER_NO_SHOW termination, but the fee falls on the driver's own trace test and I rest nothing on it. The driver's statement in the dispute record that he 'was right at the pin' carries no weight_multiplier, is contradicted by his own trace, and is not used as a carrier of any fact.

Driver compensation is not payable. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full or POL-NS-10(g) applies; neither does, and POL-NS-06 displaces the fee, so the 80 per cent payout of SGD 3.60 the Driver Advocate computes is conditional on a premise that fails. For completeness, the anti-farming check does not trip on the two figures the clause names - driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 required, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 91 is a rate of 0.022, below the 0.08 threshold - but that is not reached, because compensation is not owed in the first place. Those are the only profile fields used, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

Amount and integrity. EV-FARE-02744 carries a single SGD 4.50 cancellation-fee line and nothing else: total_charged is 4.50, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so the whole of the contested SGD 4.50 is the cancellation fee itself and the rider's success on that line is a full refund of it, not a partial one. That line equals trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and no artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d): the arrived event and the nearest fix agree within 10 seconds, the trace has no gaps across 98 fixes, the chat log's 2 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 2, and the fare reconciles. Every artifact this ruling rests on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so nothing is discounted. Escalation is not engaged: no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival in a way no clause resolves (POL-NS-01(b) and POL-NS-02 settle that question, and the driver accepts limb (b) fails on the trace), the parties' 90-day counterparty dispute counts are both 0, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, the anti-farming check does not trip, and no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence.

Ruling. The rider's claim is supported: FULL_REFUND of the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee, with no driver compensation. No clause of the policy in force produces a referral on these facts, so the referrals list is empty. Confidence is 0.95, within the 1.0 cap set by the two weight-1.0 artifacts, EV-GPS-02744 and EV-TRIP-02744, that carry the deciding facts, and above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect of SGD 4.50 is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so the refund executes on issue.

The driver's own 98-fix trace never puts him there: derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0, and his closest approach across the whole trace is derived.driver_track.min_distance_m = 53.84 m. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails, the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is not chargeable, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of it. Both the trip record and the GPS trace are COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so nothing in this finding is discounted.

Measuring the waiting period as POL-NS-01(c) requires - from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the 'I'm Here' tap - the driver's in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds (derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec = 0.0, run_count = 0) against the 180 second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180; derived.arrival.thresholds.minimum_dwell_sec = 180 for zone class STANDARD). The arrival this fee depends on is the driver's own button tap at 08:11:35 (trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker = BUTTON). POL-NS-12 makes the platform's arrival and wait-timer events a carrier independent of the exported trace only where the marker is GPS_AUTO, so it cannot rescue this arrival, and POL-NS-01(c) fixes the clock to the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix - of which this trace contains none (qualifying_fix_count = 0). A six-minute wait clock started by a tap that the driver's own trace does not corroborate cannot make the fee chargeable.

POL-NS-06(i) permits in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a present and populated advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covers the pickup road, and it expressly makes limb (i) unavailable where the advisory is MISSING. There is therefore no lawful-holding excuse and no route by which the driver's intervals could be accumulated; the shortfall stands.

In the alternative, if the Judge prefers to treat the driver as having held position outside the 50 m radius but within 400 m of the pin (his minimum distance was 53.84 m), POL-NS-03 still refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full on those facts.
